contributions.statement: If you compress agent context, keep it extractive and keep a byte-exact read-original path for files the agent will edit: even 96%-extractive compression kept solve rate within noise but tripled patch-apply failures.
contributions.evidence: §3.1: 96.0% of emitted identifiers appear in input; §6.2: 109/300 vs 122/300 resolved (McNemar p=0.079), apply failures 16 vs 5. Single-shot with oracle file context, no agent loop, vendor self-evaluation.

contributions.statement: Do the cost arithmetic before inserting a paid model as a context compressor: a frontier compressor (gpt-5) was net-negative at list prices (+$6.30 per 1M tokens), and a small compressor pays off only below a break-even self-hosting cost.
contributions.evidence: §6.3 Table 10: gpt-5 +$6.30/M vs raw, gpt-4.1-mini -$0.29/M, Paritok-4B wins only if self-host cost < $2.23/M (unmeasured); uncached pricing.

reason: Two concrete, measured cautions for any compression step (apply-failure cost of non-verbatim context; compressor cost can exceed savings). The adapter itself is Python-tuned and untested in a multi-turn agent loop, and qr must not sit in that path.
